scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Dwell magazine, modern-architecture spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad X2D 100C, 45mm f/2.8 lens, aperture f/4.0. Exterior hardwood deck staircase descending to a concrete patio at dusk, Pacific Northwest residential home. The small rectangular aluminum step light is surface-mounted flush into the riser face of the second step, at ankle level, one of three identical units spaced evenly down the stair run — a minor integrated safety detail, not the visual subject. The deck boards show genuine weathered grain, silver-gray from UV exposure, with a hairline split along one plank edge. Concrete patio below carries faint efflorescence streaking and a dried leaf pressed flat by rain. Exposure committed: the fixture's frosted glass panel clips to near-white at its center, surrounding tread surfaces stay in deep shadow with no fill. Warm 3000K glow stays strictly local — a soft pool on the riser face only; the cedar boards above read their true silver-gray, the concrete reads cool stone. Kodak Portra 400 grain throughout, 2% corner vignette, 1px chromatic aberration at the clipped fixture face. Palette: weathered silver-gray cedar, charcoal concrete, deep forest shadow, warm amber fixture glow, muted sage from distant plantings. No people, no alcohol. The fixture matches the variant reference image exactly — finish and form as shown.

scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for World of Interiors magazine, historic European residential feature; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad H6D-50c, 100mm f/2.8 lens, aperture f/3.5. Narrow stone staircase descending to a cellar or lower-ground passage in a centuries-old English country house, night. The small aluminum step light is surface-mounted into the mortar joint between two limestone risers at mid-flight — a modern safety retrofit sitting against ancient material. The limestone treads are worn concave at their centers from generations of use, with iron-oxide staining along the mortar joints and a patch of white efflorescence blooming from a damp seam in the left wall. The stone wall carries a smear of limewash that has partially flaked, revealing the raw stone beneath. Exposure committed: the frosted glass face clips fully white, the stair above and below falls into near-black with no shadow recovery. Warm 3000K glow stays local to the immediate riser and tread nose; the limestone reads its true cool buff, the mortar reads pale gray. Kodak Portra 400 grain, 3% corner vignette, 1.5px chromatic aberration at the clipped fixture. Palette: cool buff limestone, pale gray mortar, iron-oxide rust staining, near-black stair shadow, clipped warm white fixture. No people, no alcohol. The fixture matches the variant reference image exactly — finish and form as shown.
